## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical pump problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing no hydraulic load, indicating either a dry-run condition, impeller failure, or discharge line disconnection. This condition creates immediate risk of motor damage from overheating. All other components inspected during this visit are in good condition, but the pump fault prevents normal system operation and treatment.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches and comprises 22.9 percent of total tank volume, which is within the normal range. The liquid level is at the outlet.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | Intact; no visible damage |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated during this visit; soiling was light |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 HP, 115V) | **CRITICAL** | Running at 1.6A measured vs. 7.2A nameplate = 22.2% FLA. No hydraulic load detected. |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and confirmed operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals observed |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry; no ponding or breakout observed |

## PUMP DIAGNOSTIC
The effluent pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2 percent of full-load amperage indicates the pump is operating with no hydraulic load. The motor is spinning freely but not moving fluid. Possible causes include:

- Dry-run condition (tank level too low to supply the pump intake)
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Blockage in the discharge line preventing flow

A pump running without fluid load overheats rapidly and will suffer motor damage if operation continues. The pump must be inspected and the cause identified immediately.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL PRIORITY:**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. Do not operate the system until the pump has been inspected and the no-load condition has been diagnosed and corrected. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump has been repaired and normal operation is restored.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Immediate Action Required
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition that will damage the motor if left unaddressed. Stop using the system if possible and contact a service technician immediately to inspect the pump and discharge line. Do not wait for the next scheduled maintenance visit.

### Tank Solids
Your inspection revealed solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. The tank is functioning properly from a biological standpoint. Continue to keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications -- to keep solids accumulation slow and predictable.
